findings.title: Device-limit denials are cached as successful tags
findings.body: tagDeviceUI inserts the device ID into the process-local cache (default TTL about 29 minutes) before CreateOrUpdateDevice returns, and a cache hit returns nil without touching the database. CreateOrUpdateDevice now returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for an unknown device once the cap is hit, and Anonymous.Authenticate treats that error as an authentication failure. The cache entry is not removed on that error, so the next request with the same X-Grafana-Device-Id hits the cache, TagDevice returns success, and a full anonymous identity is issued even though the device was never stored and does not count toward the limit. A second in-flight request can also observe the cache entry while the first call is still in the database and be authenticated before the denial is known. After one rejected attempt, that device ID is allowed for the rest of the TTL, so the new cap does not stop anonymous access. Cache only a successful write, or cache the denial and keep returning ErrDeviceLimitReached.

findings.title: Requests without a device ID skip the cap
findings.body: The new limit is enforced only when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached and Authenticate rejects the login. TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is empty, and also returns nil when the remote address cannot be parsed as an IP, without reading AnonymousDeviceLimit. Authenticate treats that nil as success and still returns an anonymous identity with the configured org role. Any client that omits the header (API callers, the initial document request before the frontend sets the header, or a client that strips it) is never counted and never rejected. The setting therefore does not cap anonymous access; it only affects clients that voluntarily present a device ID.

findings.title: Limit check and insert are not atomic
findings.body: When deviceLimit > 0, CreateOrUpdateDevice runs SELECT COUNT(*) and, if the count is still below the limit, a separate INSERT/upsert on another session. There is no transaction, SELECT FOR UPDATE, advisory lock, or use of the existing server lock around the two steps. Concurrent first-time devices can all observe count < limit and all insert, so the number of rows in the 30-day window can exceed AnonymousDeviceLimit. A burst of new device IDs (restart, many anonymous browsers) will overshoot the configured cap. The count and the write need to be one atomic conditional insert, or held under a lock, so the limit cannot be passed.

findings.title: Wire providers changed but injector was not updated
findings.body: ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB instead of anonstore.AnonStore, and ProvideAnonDBStore gained a bare int64 deviceLimit argument. These Provide* functions are constructed by Google Wire; pkg/server/wire.go and the checked-in pkg/server/wire_gen.go are not in this PR. The generated injector still calls the old signatures, so the server package will not compile. Regeneration will also fail if ProvideAnonDBStore remains in the provider set, because Wire cannot tell which int64 should be cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. Build the store only inside ProvideAnonymousDeviceService, drop ProvideAnonDBStore from the Wire set if nothing else injects AnonStore, and commit the regenerated wire_gen.go.

findings.title: Anonymous login now blocks on untimed DB tagging
findings.body: Device tagging used to run in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and could not delay authentication. TagDevice is now called inline on the request context, which has no dedicated deadline, before an anonymous identity is returned. Every cache miss waits for an upsert, and when device_limit is set it also waits for COUNT(*) on anon_device (rows are retained for 61 days). A slow, locked, or unreachable database stalls anonymous authentication for those requests instead of bounding the tag. Put a short timeout around the call and define the timeout outcome so a database problem cannot hang anonymous traffic.

findings.title: device_limit is an undocumented ini key
findings.body: auth.anonymous.device_limit is a new operator-facing setting, defaulting to 0 via MustInt64(0). The store only enforces the cap when the value is greater than 0, so 0 means unlimited, not "allow no devices". conf/defaults.ini and the configure-grafana docs are not updated, so the key, its default, and that meaning are undiscoverable. Add it, with that comment, under [auth.anonymous] in defaults.ini and next to the other anonymous auth options.

findings.title: Limit tests never cover allow-existing or auth
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a second new device ID returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. It does not check that a device already inside the 30-day window is still updated and allowed when the count is at the limit, which is the updateDevice path every returning user depends on. No test calls TagDevice or Anonymous.Authenticate with a non-zero limit, so a local-cache hit that turns a limit error into a successful anonymous login, or a missing X-Grafana-Device-Id that skips the cap, would not fail CI. Add a store test for the at-limit refresh of an existing device and a service test that a new device is denied on every attempt while an already-counted one still authenticates.
